_transcription: Booklet is 31 pages (idx 0-30) and strictly alternating: idx 0 cover, idx 1 Hindi instructions, then ENGLISH on every EVEN index 2-30 and HINDI on every ODD index 1-29. Measured, not assumed: the top 30% of all fifteen odd pages (1,3,5,...,29) was montaged and every one opens in Devanagari, so there is NO English overflow onto an odd top and NO mid-paper parity inversion; the last page (idx 30) is even and English. Corroborated by content continuity - every English page resumes exactly where the previous English page stopped (p04 ends Q5 / p06 opens Q6 ... p28 ends Q33(a) OR / p30 opens Q33(b)), with no numbering jump anywhere. Decimal points: the paper prints RAISED dots throughout (constants list on idx 2: 6.63, 1.6, 8.854, 9.1, 1.675, 1.673, 6.023, 1.38; and 0.5 A, 2.0, 5.0 m, 0.6 mm, 0.2 m in the questions), so every decimal is written 0{\cdot}5. The marking scheme (20 pages, header 'SUBJECT NAME PHYSICS (PAPER CODE 55/4/3)') prints ordinary baseline dots - the PAPER is followed, per the addendum. Structure agrees with the paper's own General Instructions (33 questions; A 1-16 MCQ @1, B 17-21 @2, C 22-28 @3, D 29-30 case study @4, E 31-33 @5 = 70). Instruction (viii) gives NO internal-choice count ('in few questions in all the Sections except Section A'), so the alternatives roster was built by walking the whole marking scheme for a bare OR on its own line and confirming each against a printed OR on the paper page: seven of them, at Q21, Q27, Q29(iv), Q30(iv), Q31, Q32, Q33. 26 keyed MCQs - 16 in Section A plus 10 in Section D - all taken verbatim from the scheme and uppercased, none derived. The WHOLE scheme was read (ms p00-p19) and contains ZERO void notes: no 'award full mark', no 'no option is correct', no 'mere attempt', no dual key, no medium-specific award.

questions.subtopic: Bohr Model of the Hydrogen Atom
questions.context:
A hydrogen atom consists of an electron revolving in a circular orbit of radius r with certain velocity v around a proton located at the nucleus of the atom. The electrostatic force of attraction between the revolving electron and the proton provides the requisite centripetal force to keep it in the orbit. According to Bohr's model, an electron can revolve only in certain stable orbits. The angular momentum of the electron in these orbits is some integral multiple of \(\dfrac{h}{2\pi}\), where h is the Planck's constant.
Further, when an electron makes a transition from one orbit of higher energy to that of lower energy, a photon is emitted having energy equal to the difference between energies of the initial and final states. Assuming the mass and charge of an electron as m and e respectively, answer the following questions.

Since the hall is large enough, interference pattern is formed on the wall \(5{\cdot}0\) m from the slits. For clear and comfortable view by all the students they want the fringe width 5 mm.
(I) Find the slit separation for obtaining the desired interference pattern.
(II) How far will the first minimum be from the central maximum ?

(ii) Three point charges of – 2 nC, – 1 nC, and + 5 nC are kept at the vertices A, B and C of an equilateral triangle of side \(0{\cdot}2\) m. Find the total amount of work done in shifting the charges from A to \(A_1\), B to \(B_1\) and C to \(C_1\). Here \(A_1\), \(B_1\) and \(C_1\) are the midpoints of sides AB, BC and CA, respectively.

(i) Show that Gauss's theorem is consistent with Coulomb's law. Using it, derive an expression for the electric field due to a uniformly charged thin spherical shell of radius r at a point at a distance y from the centre of the shell such that (I) \(y > r\), and (II) \(y < r\).
(ii) A point charge of \(+2\) nC is kept at the origin of a three-dimensional coordinate system. Find the type and magnitude of the charge which should be kept at (0, 0, – 6m) so that the potential due to the system becomes zero at (0, 0, 2m).

questions.subtopic: Lenz's Law and Conservation of Energy
questions.stem:
(i) State Lenz's law and explain how this law is a consequence of conservation of energy principle.
(ii) A square shaped loop of side \(\dfrac{l}{2}\) is initially lying outside a region of uniform magnetic field \(\vec{B}\) as shown in the figure. The loop is moved towards right with a constant velocity \(\vec{v}\) till it goes out of the region of magnetic field.
(I) What will be the directions of induced current when the loop enters the field and when it leaves the field ?
(II) Draw the plots showing the variation of magnetic flux \(\phi\) linked with the loop with time t and variation of induced emf E with time t. Mark the relevant values of E, \(\phi\) and t on the graphs.
questions._figure: REQUIRED — sub-part (II) asks for the RELEVANT VALUES of \(\phi\), E and t to be marked, and those depend on two lengths the stem never states: the width of the field region and how far the loop starts from its left edge. Both exist only in the drawing. Read off this paper's own page: a tall vertical band of crosses captioned \(\vec{B}\) at its head and measured \(l\) wide by a horizontal arrow at its foot; to its left a small square of side \(\dfrac{l}{2}\), that side marked by a vertical arrow, with a horizontal arrow \(\vec{v}\) pointing right and a second horizontal measure \(l\) running from the square across to the band's left edge; and to the right of the band a dashed square with a short arrow, showing the loop after it has emerged. DELIBERATELY WITHHELD: nothing about the sense of the induced current, which is what sub-part (I) asks for and which the drawing does not show. Page idx 28.

questions.stem:
(i) Differentiate between peak and rms values of alternating current. How are they related ?
(ii) A current element X is connected across an ac source of emf \(V = V_0 \sin 2\pi\nu t\). It is found that the voltage leads the current in phase by \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\) radian. If element X was replaced by element Y, the voltage lags behind the current in phase by \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\) radian.
(I) Identify elements X and Y by drawing phasor diagrams.
(II) Obtain the condition of resonance when both elements X and Y are connected in series to the source and obtain expression for resonant frequency. What is the impedance value in this case ?
